sentences.text: The Bermuda hawk was an extinct bird of prey found only on the island of Bermuda, and it was the sole species within the genus Bermuteo. The genus name Bermuteo combines the name of the island with the genus Buteo, which contains many hawk and buzzard species.

The species name avivorus indicates that the bird engaged in catching other birds. Its femur had a uniquely flattened head shape that was smaller and less round than those of other hawk genera. The distinct wing-like condyle found on the femurs of most Accipitridae birds is reduced in the Bermuda hawk.
Based on bone comparisons, the Bermuda hawk likely ranged in mass from approximately 244g to 495g.
Historical accounts describe the Bermuda hawk as tame enough to be clubbed by explorers.
Captain John Smith reported a lack of endemic hawks in 1623, suggesting the species had gone extinct by then.

The species Bermuteo avivorus was described by Storrs Lovejoy Olson in 2008. Subfossil remains of the Bermuda hawk were found in quaternary deposits on the island of Bermuda. The original sample used to describe the species consisted of seven bones from four or five locations, representing at most six individuals.
The Bermuda hawk likely fed almost exclusively on other birds due to the abundance of endemic bird populations in Bermuda.
Researchers inferred that females of the Bermuda hawk may have been twice as heavy as males.
Native evergreen forests of Bermuda cedar and palmetto likely served as habitat for the Bermuda hawk before human settlement.
The Bermuda hawk is classified within the family Accipitridae and belongs to the subfamily Buteoninae.
The Bermuda hawk lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, between 0.129 and 0 million years ago.

The exact date of extinction is unknown, though 1603 is cited based on explorer sightings. Hunting and the introduction of invasive species like feral pigs in the 17th century likely caused the extinction of the Bermuda hawk. Deforestation and burning of native forests after European settlement may have contributed to the hawk's extinction.
